title: Applications of Derivatives
subject: Mathematics
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET • Rapid Revision Deck

cards.q: Slopes of Tangent and Normal to curve y = f(x) at P(x₁, y₁)?
cards.a:
Slope of tangent: m = (dy/dx) at (x₁, y₁).
Slope of normal: m' = -1 / m = -1 / (dy/dx) at (x₁, y₁).
cards.hint: Normal is perpendicular to tangent, so m · m' = -1.

cards.q: Equations of Tangent and Normal lines at point P(x₁, y₁)?
cards.a:
Tangent: y - y₁ = m (x - x₁)
Normal: y - y₁ = (-1/m) (x - x₁).
cards.hint: If m = 0, tangent is horizontal (y = y₁); if m = ∞, tangent is vertical (x = x₁).

cards.q: Conditions for tangent to be parallel to x-axis and parallel to y-axis?
cards.a:
Parallel to x-axis: dy/dx = 0 (horizontal tangent).
Parallel to y-axis (perpendicular to x-axis): dx/dy = 0 or dy/dx = ±∞ (vertical tangent).
cards.hint: MHT-CET standard question: find points on curve where tangent is horizontal.

cards.q: Angle of intersection θ between two curves with slopes m₁ and m₂?
cards.a:
tan θ = | (m₁ - m₂) / (1 + m₁ m₂) |.
Orthogonal (perpendicular) curves: m₁ · m₂ = -1.
cards.hint: Curves cut orthogonally if product of their tangent slopes at intersection equals -1.

cards.q: Derivative as a Rate Measure: Velocity and Acceleration?
cards.a:
If s = f(t) is displacement at time t:
Velocity: v = ds/dt
Acceleration: a = dv/dt = d²s/dt².
cards.hint: Particle comes to instantaneous rest or reverses direction when v = 0.

cards.q: Related rates: Volume and Surface Area of a Sphere of radius r?
cards.a:
Volume: V = (4/3) π r³ ⇒ dV/dt = 4 π r² (dr/dt)
Surface Area: S = 4 π r² ⇒ dS/dt = 8 π r (dr/dt).
cards.hint: Note that dV/dt = S · (dr/dt). Instantaneous rate of volume change equals surface area times radial speed.

cards.q: Formula for Approximations using differentials?
cards.a: f(a + h) ≈ f(a) + h · f'(a), where h is a small increment (positive or negative).
cards.hint: Choose 'a' as a nearby value where f(a) and f'(a) can be calculated easily.

cards.q: State Rolle's Theorem and its 3 mandatory conditions.
cards.a:
If f(x) is: (1) continuous on [a, b], (2) differentiable on (a, b), and (3) f(a) = f(b),
then there exists at least one c ∈ (a, b) such that f'(c) = 0.
cards.hint: Geometrically: There is at least one point where the tangent is horizontal (parallel to x-axis).

cards.q: Trap in Rolle's Theorem: Interval type for c?
cards.a: c must lie in the OPEN interval (a, b), never at the endpoints a or b! (a < c < b).
cards.hint: If an algebraic solution yields c = a or c = b, it MUST be discarded!

cards.q: State Lagrange's Mean Value Theorem (LMVT).
cards.a:
If f(x) is: (1) continuous on [a, b], (2) differentiable on (a, b),
then there exists at least one c ∈ (a, b) such that f'(c) = [ f(b) - f(a) ] / (b - a).
cards.hint: Geometrically: There is at least one tangent parallel to the chord joining endpoints (a, f(a)) and (b, f(b)).

cards.q: Condition for a function f(x) to be Strictly Increasing or Decreasing?
cards.a:
Strictly Increasing on (a, b): f'(x) > 0 for all x ∈ (a, b).
Strictly Decreasing on (a, b): f'(x) < 0 for all x ∈ (a, b).
cards.hint: Non-decreasing: f'(x) ≥ 0; Non-increasing: f'(x) ≤ 0.

cards.q: What is a Stationary Point vs a Critical Point?
cards.a:
Stationary Point: Point x = c where f'(c) = 0.
Critical Point: Point x = c in domain where EITHER f'(c) = 0 OR f'(c) does not exist.
cards.hint: Every stationary point is a critical point, but not vice-versa (e.g. x = 0 for f(x) = |x| is critical, not stationary).

cards.q: First Derivative Test for Local Maxima and Minima?
cards.a:
Let f'(c) = 0:
1. If f'(x) changes sign from + to - as x passes through c ⇒ Local MAXIMUM at c.
2. If f'(x) changes sign from - to + as x passes through c ⇒ Local MINIMUM at c.
3. If f'(x) does not change sign ⇒ Point of Inflection.
cards.hint: Positive to negative means curve was climbing then descending, forming a peak (maximum).

cards.q: Second Derivative Test for Local Maxima and Minima?
cards.a:
Let f'(c) = 0:
If f''(c) < 0 ⇒ Local MAXIMUM at x = c.
If f''(c) > 0 ⇒ Local MINIMUM at x = c.
cards.hint: Mnemonic: Negative second derivative indicates concave down (frown = peak = max).

cards.q: What happens if f'(c) = 0 and f''(c) = 0?
cards.a: The Second Derivative Test FAILS (inconclusive). You must fall back to the First Derivative Test or test higher derivatives.
cards.hint: Example: For f(x) = x⁴ at x = 0, f''(0) = 0, but it has a minimum by 1st derivative test.

cards.q: How to find Global (Absolute) Maxima and Minima on a closed interval [a, b]?
cards.a:
1. Find all critical points in (a, b).
2. Calculate f(x) at these critical points AND at the two endpoints a and b.
3. The greatest value is Absolute Maximum; smallest is Absolute Minimum.
cards.hint: Absolute extrema frequently occur at endpoints where derivative is non-zero!

cards.q: What is a Point of Inflection?
cards.a: A point on the curve where the concavity changes (concave upwards ↔ concave downwards). Condition: f''(x) = 0 and f''(x) changes sign.
cards.hint: At a point of inflection, the tangent line crosses (cuts through) the curve.

cards.q: Concave Upwards vs Concave Downwards conditions?
cards.a:
Concave Upwards (convex): f''(x) > 0 on the interval.
Concave Downwards (concave): f''(x) < 0 on the interval.
cards.hint: Concave up holds water (cup); concave down spills water (cap).

cards.q: MHT-CET Optimization Shortcut: Rectangle of maximum area inscribed in a circle of radius R?
cards.a: It is always a SQUARE of side R √2, and its maximum area is 2 R².
cards.hint: Symmetry rule: For perimeter/area extrema, regular shapes (squares, equilateral triangles) always win!

cards.q: MHT-CET Optimization Shortcut: Open box made by cutting equal corner squares of side x from sheet of dimensions L × B?
cards.a: Maximum volume occurs when x = [ (L + B) - √(L² - L B + B²) ] / 6.
cards.hint: For a square sheet (L = B): x = L / 6, and Max Volume = 2 L³ / 27.

cards.q: MHT-CET Shortcut: Divide positive number S into two parts x and y such that xᵐ yⁿ is maximum?
cards.a: The parts must be in the ratio of their powers: x / m = y / n ⇒ x = m S / (m + n), y = n S / (m + n).
cards.hint: Direct 5-second trick! Avoid setting up full derivative and second derivative.

cards.q: Lengths of Subtangent and Subnormal to curve y = f(x)?
cards.a:
Length of Subtangent = | y / (dy/dx) | = | y / m |
Length of Subnormal = | y · (dy/dx) | = | y · m |.
cards.hint: Subtangent divides by slope m; subnormal multiplies by slope m.

cards.q: Condition for function f(x) = a x³ + b x² + c x + d to be monotonic for all x ∈ R?
cards.a: f'(x) = 3a x² + 2b x + c must have discriminant Δ ≤ 0 ⇒ 4b² - 12ac ≤ 0 ⇒ b² ≤ 3ac.
cards.hint: If discriminant is ≤ 0, derivative never changes sign, so f(x) is strictly monotonic.

cards.q: Ladder sliding against vertical wall problem: relation between speeds?
cards.a: If ladder length is L: x² + y² = L² ⇒ 2x (dx/dt) + 2y (dy/dt) = 0 ⇒ dy/dt = - (x/y) · (dx/dt).
cards.hint: dy/dt is negative because height y decreases as foot x slides away (dx/dt > 0).

cards.q: Shortest distance between a point (x₀, y₀) and a curve y = f(x)?
cards.a: The line segment of shortest distance lies along the NORMAL to the curve passing through (x₀, y₀).
cards.hint: Shortest distance between any two non-intersecting smooth curves is along their common normal.
